// scheduler.rs — ordinary Rust, no attack content whatsoever.
// "inst" is used here purely as an abbreviation for "instance"/"index",
// the way it commonly appears in real codebases — not as any reference
// to a model control token.

struct TaskQueue {
    tasks: Vec<u32>,
}

fn run_task(tasks: &[u32], inst: usize) -> u32 {
    tasks[inst]
}

fn swap_tasks(table: &mut [u32], inst: usize, other: usize) {
    table.swap(inst, other);
}

fn main() {
    let tasks = vec![10, 20, 30, 40];
    let inst = 2;
    println!("task at index {} is {}", inst, run_task(&tasks, inst));

    let mut table = vec![1, 2, 3];
    swap_tasks(&mut table, inst, 0);
}
